solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: On the counter, it’s cutting through dirt? (7)

annotation.definition: On the counter, it’s cutting through dirt?

indicatorNotes.On the counter: running counter means going backwards, so IT'S is read right to left
indicatorNotes.cutting through: the reversed letters slice into the middle of the dirt

blocks.note: dung = dirt, muck
IT'S written backwards

annotation.surface: A cleaning tip about wiping the kitchen worktop.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'counter' is a kitchen worktop in the surface and a backwards instruction in the wordplay, and dusting a counter really does cut through dirt.
annotation.definitionFit: Dusting is the cleaning done on a counter to clear away dirt.

entries.clue: Shuffle diamonds, with more out there (6)

blocks.note: D = diamonds, the card suit
odder = more strange, more 'out there'

annotation.surface: Card-table advice to shuffle the diamonds with some stranger cards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' looks like an instruction to rearrange cards, but it is the definition: to dodder is to shuffle along unsteadily.
annotation.definitionFit: To dodder is to walk with shaky, shuffling steps.

entries.clue: Dubious unique selling point adopted by religious group (7)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: the group takes the selling point in, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a sect is a religious group
USP is the marketing abbreviation for unique selling point

annotation.surface: A cult whose marketing pitch looks a little shady.
annotation.walkthrough: USP is a standard marketing abbreviation; it goes between the S and ECT of SECT.
annotation.definitionFit: Suspect as an adjective means dubious, open to doubt.

entries.clue: Travel from place to place, furious about something of a fork (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the furious word goes around the fork part

blocks.note: irate = furious
a tine is one prong of a fork

annotation.surface: An angry traveller who has lost a fork on the road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something of a fork' is a roundabout way of naming a part of it: one prong, a tine.
annotation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to travel from place to place, as a circuit preacher or judge does.

entries.clue: Lecher caught hugging American (4)

indicatorNotes.hugging: the word for caught wraps its arms around the A

blocks.note: got = caught, as in 'got the thief'
A = American

annotation.surface: A lecher arrested while clinging to an American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is usually C in crosswords; here it is the whole word GOT.
annotation.definitionFit: An old goat is a lecherous man.

entries.clue: Pop star Simon admits, finally, Garfunkel wrote in a distinct way (7)

indicatorNotes.admits: the pop star lets the other letters in
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: Carly Simon, the American singer-songwriter
last letters of GarfunkeL and wrotE

annotation.surface: Gossip about which Simon really wrote the songs, Paul Simon's partner Garfunkel or someone else.
annotation.walkthrough: Next to Garfunkel, 'Simon' wants to be Paul Simon, but the pop star here is Carly Simon.
annotation.definitionFit: Clearly means in a distinct, easily seen way.

entries.clue: Characters from Greece and America taking in someone sitting with an ape (10)

indicatorNotes.taking in: the two letter names surround the rest

blocks.note: chi is a Greek letter; zee is how Americans say Z
an MP is a sitting member of Parliament
used as written

annotation.surface: Letters from two countries, and someone who ends up sitting next to an ape.
annotation.walkthrough: Members of Parliament are said to sit for a constituency, which is why 'someone sitting' is a stock crossword phrase. The Greek and American characters are spelt-out letter names.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the chimp is one of the great apes, the closest living relative of humans.

entries.clue: Lack of interest continues somehow to overlook terrible cost (5)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters of continues are to be arranged in some other way
indicatorNotes.terrible: the letters of cost can appear in any order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
these four letters are removed, in any order

annotation.surface: Boredom drags on, and nobody minds an awful price.
annotation.walkthrough: Take C, O, S and T out of CONTINUES and the five letters left, N I N U E, rearrange to ENNUI.
annotation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a lack of interest in anything.

entries.clue: Composer almost climbed biblical mount, losing acceleration (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

blocks.note: ROSE = climbed, minus its last letter
SINAI, the mountain of the Ten Commandments, minus A (acceleration)

annotation.surface: A composer who nearly made it up Sinai but ran out of speed.
annotation.walkthrough: A = acceleration comes from physics notation.
annotation.definitionFit: Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

entries.clue: English newspaper of yore originally erected American national park (8)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letters of 'of yore'
indicatorNotes.erected: in a down answer, set upright means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: E = English
The Times, the paper this puzzle comes from
first letters of Of Yore

annotation.surface: An old English newspaper that once set up an American national park.
annotation.walkthrough: E + TIMES + OY is built first, then the whole string is turned upside down, which a down answer shows as reading bottom to top.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Californian valley of granite cliffs and waterfalls is one of the best-known US national parks.

entries.clue: Stop being humble after abandoning second island country (11)

indicatorNotes.after abandoning: the humble word has let go of the letters for second

blocks.note: MODEST = being humble, without MO (a second, a short moment)
I = island
a nation is a country

annotation.surface: Advice to give up modesty once you have left a second island nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop being humble' reads as one instruction, but 'Stop' alone is the definition. MO = second, as in 'wait a mo'.
annotation.definitionFit: A destination is a stop, a place where a journey ends.

entries.clue: Relative Strangers employing Baranski ultimately for body (3)

indicatorNotes.employing: the word Strangers takes on the new letter
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is used
indicatorNotes.for body: the new letter stands in for the body, the middle of the word between its first and last letters

blocks.note: STRANGERS with its body TRANGER removed, leaving S…S
last letter of BaranskI

annotation.surface: A cast note about a film called Relative Strangers starring Christine Baranski.
annotation.walkthrough: The body of STRANGERS is everything between its first and last letters; the I from Baranski replaces it. Christine Baranski is an American actress.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the informal short form of sister names one kind of relative.

entries.clue: This clue is featured in channel eventually (6)

indicatorNotes.is featured in: the answer appears inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: channEL EVENtually

annotation.surface: A remark that this clue will turn up on some channel eventually.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This clue' is the definition because the clue is numbered 11.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue sits at 11 across, so 'this clue' is eleven.

entries.clue: Plump one is repeatedly clinging to society for positivity (8)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: repeatedly means more than once, so the contraction for 'one is' appears twice
indicatorNotes.clinging to: the second copy holds on around the S

blocks.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
one is = I'M, written twice
S = society

annotation.surface: A plump person who keeps clinging to society in a hopeful way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective about weight but is the verb, as in 'plump for'. Only the second copy of the contraction does the clinging.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hopeful, look-on-the-bright-side outlook is positivity.

entries.clue: Render topless boyfriend, maybe retaining speed about it (10)

indicatorNotes.retaining: the boyfriend word keeps the other letters inside

blocks.note: a date may be a boyfriend
PACE = speed, turned around
used as written

annotation.surface: Undressing a boyfriend quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Render topless' suggests stripping, but the top removed is a head.
annotation.definitionFit: To decapitate is to cut off the head, leaving the body topless.

entries.clue: Tube driver perhaps ruined station in a rage (5,8)

indicatorNotes.in a rage: the letters are thrown about wildly

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: An Underground train driver furious about a wrecked station.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, whose drivers belong to a union famous for strikes; 'perhaps' marks the driver as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A Tube driver is typically a union member, one example of a trade unionist.

entries.clue: Oscar phoned employee of publisher, missing cover’s drink (9)

indicatorNotes.missing cover: the outer letters are stripped away

blocks.note: O = Oscar in the phonetic alphabet
rang = phoned
a READER assesses manuscripts for a publisher; without its first and last letters it is EADE

annotation.surface: An Oscar winner who rang an editor about a book jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' fits the publishing surface as a book jacket, but here it means the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink is one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Certainly mean to carry Australian creature away from the south (3,5)

indicatorNotes.to carry: the mean word holds the creature inside
indicatorNotes.away from the south: in a down answer, moving away from the bottom means reading upwards

blocks.note: tight = mean with money

blocks.clueFragment: Australian creature away from the south
blocks.note: ROO, short for kangaroo, going upwards

annotation.surface: Someone stingy set on carrying a kangaroo north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too right' is emphatic agreement, mostly Australian and British; the Australian creature fits that flavour.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the emphatic Australian and British exclamation of agreement works as 'certainly!' in reply to a remark.

entries.clue: Failing to read ahead in agreement? (2,3,4,4)

blocks.note: a literal picture of a reader who has not turned over
the idiom for agreeing

annotation.surface: A slow reader who never skips ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal, playful reading of the idiom; the question mark flags it.
annotation.definitionFit: People on the same page share an understanding, so they are in agreement.

entries.clue: Measure around outside of uniform’s pocket (7)

indicatorNotes.around: the measure word is turned round
indicatorNotes.outside of: the turned word goes outside the uniform letter

blocks.note: RESORT = a measure, as in 'last resort', turned round
U = uniform in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Taking a tape measure round the outside of a uniform pocket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' is the verb: to trouser money is to pocket it. The tailoring surface makes 'measure' look like a tape measure.
annotation.definitionFit: To trouser something is to pocket it, often dishonestly.

entries.clue: Earl unfortunately let slip cutting line in letter (7)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: the letters of the phrase have come out badly arranged
indicatorNotes.cutting: cutting a letter means snipping it off, so the L for line is removed from the phrase

blocks.note: E = Earl
LETSLIP minus one L (line)

annotation.surface: An earl who has unluckily blurted something out in a letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let slip' reads as a phrase meaning blurted, but it is just letters to rearrange once an L is gone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, usually for a formal or biblical letter, like the New Testament letters of Paul.

entries.clue: Cross as your old and new wife stripped together (6)

indicatorNotes.stripped: each word loses an outer letter

blocks.note: THY = your in old English, without its T
BRIDE = new wife, without its E

annotation.surface: Someone annoyed that an ex and a new wife have been undressed together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the noun: a cross between two breeds.
annotation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a cross between two species or varieties.

entries.clue: Hero said to adjust former state (8)

indicatorNotes.to adjust: the letters are to be altered into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A hero declaring that an old state must change.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhodesia was the name of the country that is now Zimbabwe.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhodesia is a state that no longer exists under that name.

entries.clue: New partner no longer mounted paintings? (5)

indicatorNotes.mounted: in a down answer, climbing means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
ART = paintings, going upwards

annotation.surface: A new partner no longer hanging pictures on the wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mounted paintings' reads as pictures put up in frames; 'mounted' instead turns ART upwards. 'New' means additional, as in 'new recruits'.
annotation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, which is what new means in 'new staff'.

entries.clue: Make unpleasant fruit fancy on the outside (6)

blocks.note: an ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
outer letters of FancY

annotation.surface: A fruit that looks posh from outside but spoils things.
annotation.walkthrough: The ugli fruit, a tangelo, is named for its rough skin, so it nearly gives the answer away.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the verb means to make ugly, and ugly things are unpleasant to look at.

entries.clue: High shot of centre stage (4)

indicatorNotes.shot of centre: to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so the middle letter goes

blocks.note: steep = high, as in a steep price
the middle letter of the five, an E, is removed

annotation.surface: A camera angle from above on the middle of a stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a camera shot; here it is 'shot of', meaning rid of.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: each stage of a process or plan is one step towards its end.

entries.clue: Rabbit periodically ignored grass (3)

blocks.note: G r A s S, keeping letters 1, 3 and 5

annotation.surface: A rabbit that at times left the grass alone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is a verb: to rabbit on is to chatter, and so is to gas.
annotation.definitionFit: To rabbit and to gas both mean to talk idly at length.

entries.clue: Who introduces Mike and Daisy after perfectly introducing son? (11)

indicatorNotes.introducing: to introduce something is to put it in, so the son letter goes inside the phrase for perfectly
indicatorNotes.after: Mike and Daisy come after the rest

blocks.note: to a T = perfectly
S = son
M = Mike in the phonetic alphabet
an aster is a daisy-like flower

annotation.surface: A host at a party introducing a couple and their son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mike and Daisy' look like guests' names, but they are a phonetic-alphabet letter and a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A toastmaster introduces the speakers at a formal dinner.

entries.clue: Offend one following tense row (7)

indicatorNotes.following: the offend and one pieces come after the tense letter

blocks.note: T = tense, the grammar abbreviation
to err is to sin, to offend
an ace is a one on a card

annotation.surface: Insulting someone after a tense argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel next to 'tense', but it is a row of houses: a terrace in British usage.
annotation.definitionFit: British usage: a terrace is a row of houses joined wall to wall along a street.

entries.clue: Cod sandwich shop informally closing (7)

indicatorNotes.informally: the shop's name is cut to its everyday short form

blocks.note: Pret A Manger, a British sandwich chain, known as Pret
the closing is the end

annotation.surface: A fish sandwich shop that is shutting down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish in a sandwich, but as an adjective it means fake, as in 'cod philosophy'.
annotation.definitionFit: Cod as an adjective means sham or pretend.
